approved_scope: Jeremiah 31:19 and Luke 17:4 in POB and Simplified POB only. Keep Mark 1:15 and 2 Corinthians 7:10 unchanged. Preserve earlier policy plan and revision history.

records.before_text: For after I turned back[d][a], I felt regret; and after I was instructed, I struck my thigh. I was ashamed, and also humiliated[c][b], because I bore the disgrace of my youth.
records.after_text: For after I turned away[a], I was sorry for what I had done[d]; and after I was instructed, I struck my thigh. I was ashamed, and also humiliated[c][b], because I bore the disgrace of my youth.
records.after_text_without_policy_anchor: For after I turned away[a], I was sorry for what I had done; and after I was instructed, I struck my thigh. I was ashamed, and also humiliated[c][b], because I bore the disgrace of my youth.
records.rationale: Use the maintainer-selected turning-away reading of shuv, retaining turning back as an alternative. Render nacham as sorrow over wrongdoing; "for what I had done" is contextual clarification, not a separate Hebrew phrase. No added degree of sorrow is intended.

records.before_text: And if he sins against you seven times in a day[a], and seven times returns to you saying[c][b], ‘I am reorienting[d] myself,’ you shall forgive him.
records.after_text: And if he sins against you seven times in a day[a], and seven times returns to you saying[c][b], ‘I am changing my ways[d],’ you shall forgive him.
records.after_text_without_policy_anchor: And if he sins against you seven times in a day[a], and seven times returns to you saying[c][b], ‘I am changing my ways,’ you shall forgive him.
records.rationale: Use natural first-person dialogue for metanoo: "I am changing my ways." This expresses the speaker's stated change of disposition and conduct, not independently verified or completed moral transformation. Preserve the separate return-to-you verb and the command to forgive.
